CAT.rationale: CAT presents a case of strong business momentum offset by stretched and deteriorating valuation quality. The earnings trajectory is unambiguously positive — +30% YoY EPS growth is not trivial. However, the market has re-rated the stock from ~20x to ~40x PE while net margins have actually *fallen* from 15.7% to 13.3%. At a 2.5% earnings yield versus a 4.68% 10-year Treasury, and with a leveraged balance sheet (D/E ~4.1x), the quantitative risk-reward skews unattractive. The stock is not expensive relative to its own recent peak (52.6x PE), but it is expensive relative to the earnings quality and balance-sheet resilience of the underlying business. On a pure fundamental-attractiveness basis — earnings durability, margin trajectory, cash generation, and valuation versus own history — CAT is not quantitatively attractive at current levels. The business is performing; the price has more than compensated for it.
